        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Keyv and Cacheable npm packages compromised in active supply-chain attack]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/keyv-and-cacheable-npm-packages-compromised-in-active-supply-chain-attack</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.38ac1722-5021-42b6-8781-dc66506c38e4</guid>
            <pubDate>Tue, 04 Aug 2026 17:11:36 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[On August 4, 2026, a self-propagating worm began publishing malicious versions of the npm packages keyv and cacheable and their common dependencies. This keyv/cacheable supply-chain attack, tracked as keyv-shai-hulud, is still developing as we publish, and the list of affected npm packages has grown through the day. Below we cover what we know so far, how to check whether your organization is exposed, and the controls that stop this class of attack from reaching your builds.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[The evolution of Shai-Hulud-style worms]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/evolution-of-shai-hulud-worms</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.02cff090-224a-478a-9e9a-714b21642a32</guid>
            <pubDate>Thu, 30 Jul 2026 14:18:08 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[A chronological teardown of the Shai-Hulud worm lineage (including the Mini Shai-Hulud, Miasma, and Hades variants). Learn how subsequent actors bypassed static scanners using Github Actions memory scraping, native build hooks, trojan binary extensions, and LLM analysis misdirection across npm, PyPI, RubyGems, and Docker.]]></description>
        </item>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Inside the AsyncAPI npm supply chain attack]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/inside-the-asyncapi-npm-supply-chain-attack</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.d650fb20-33bc-470d-9240-f643f6f9a4cf</guid>
            <pubDate>Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:22:17 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[On July 14th, an attacker hijacked AsyncAPI's own CI/CD pipeline to publish four trojanized npm packages under a trusted namespace – reaching 2.9 million weekly downloads before anyone noticed. No bad reputation, no known-malicious version, nothing for conventional defenses to catch. Here's how it happened, and what would have stopped it.]]></description>

        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[A dependency firewall gives your scanner better inputs]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/a-dependency-firewall-gives-your-scanner-better-inputs</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.0151bf0b-5f1e-4607-9f92-2748285e87f2</guid>
            <pubDate>Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[Modern supply chain attacks don't exploit vulnerable code – they target trusted packages and execute before any scanner runs. Here's the structural gap behind every missed malicious package, and where the control point should actually be.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Start secure, stay secure with WizOS and Cloudsmith]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/start-secure-stay-secure-with-wizos-and-cloudsmith</link>

            <pubDate>Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[Hardened container base images only fix the security problem if every team actually pulls them. Together, WizOS and Cloudsmith enables teams to use images compiled from source with SLA-backed CVE patching, served through the registry URL developers already use.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Dependency attacks start before your scanner runs]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/dependency-attacks-start-before-your-scanner-runs</link>

            <pubDate>Tue, 23 Jun 2026 12:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[Most security tooling catches threats after packages already enter your environment. A leaked npm key reveals why that timing matters, and where enforcement needs to happen instead.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Cloudsmith credentials are now detectable by GitHub Secret Scanning]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/cloudsmith-credentials-are-now-detectable-by-github-secret-scanning</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.9317a9ff-8db7-4267-8bec-5b8f2a898cc7</guid>
            <pubDate>Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[Cloudsmith API keys carry a unique prefix that GitHub's secret scanning infrastructure recognizes. Teams get direct notification the moment a credential is detected in a repository – no extra tooling, no process changes required.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Authenticate to Cloudsmith with your Google Cloud identity]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/authenticate-to-cloudsmith-with-your-google-cloud-identity</link>

            <pubDate>Wed, 17 Jun 2026 12:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[Long-lived API keys create rotation debt and leak risk. If your workloads run on Google Cloud, you can authenticate to Cloudsmith using existing service account identities and short-lived OIDC tokens instead.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[Inside the Mastra npm supply chain attack]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/inside-the-mastra-npm-supply-chain-attack</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.7ed99928-47cd-4cb0-b0b1-8c160291d60b</guid>
            <pubDate>Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:30:39 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[On June 17, a typosquatted npm package and stolen contributor credentials gave attackers access to 144 Mastra packages with nearly a million weekly downloads. Here's how the attack unfolded, how the malware evaded detection, and how to protect your pipeline.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[How Cloudsmith's cooldown policies stop newly published packages without disrupting your builds]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/how-cloudsmith-cooldown-policies-block-newly-published-packages-without-disrupting-your-builds</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.ee5fc006-744a-4188-be4a-e0b45c8b9525</guid>
            <pubDate>Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[Cloudsmith enforces cooldown policies at the index level using policy as code, so your package manager resolves to compliant npm, Python, Go, Maven, and NuGet versions automatically – no broken builds required.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[From trusted artifact to controlled deployment: Cloudsmith and Octopus Deploy]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/from-trusted-artifact-to-controlled-deployment-cloudsmith-and-octopus-deploy</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.3255e82b-cd2e-448d-b770-2330589b7f01</guid>
            <pubDate>Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[The gap between "is this artifact trustworthy?" and "how does it get deployed?" is where most governance breaks down. Cloudsmith and Octopus Deploy cover that full journey, with a clean policy handoff between them.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[The EU Cyber Resilience Act: What engineering teams need to do to be compliant]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/the-eu-cyber-resilience-act-what-engineering-teams-need-to-do-to-be-compliant</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.2f54ae85-5c7a-45d0-a71b-3a1b55094ad1</guid>
            <pubDate>Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:26:09 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[The EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation EU 2024/2847) is the first EU-wide regulation that places mandatory cybersecurity requirements on digital products throughout their entire lifecycle, from design and development all the way through deployment and end-of-life.]]></description>
        </item>
        <item>
            <title><![CDATA[How artifact management closes the gaps that leave you exposed under the CRA]]></title>
            <link>https://cloudsmith.com/blog/how-artifact-management-closes-the-gaps-that-leave-you-exposed-under-the-cra</link>
            <guid isPermaLink="false">tag:cloudsmith.com,2019:blog.b4de63e1-d0c7-47b9-b51a-668c02449b8e</guid>
            <pubDate>Tue, 09 Jun 2026 16:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
            <description><![CDATA[The Cyber Resilience Act reaches beyond product security into the components inside what you ship like the open-source packages your team pulled, or the transitive dependencies nobody explicitly chose. Fragmented artifact practices aren't just operational debt; they're a structural compliance liability.]]></description>
        </item>
